sentence: The urinary bladder is a muscular organ in the pelvis that stores the urine sent down from the kidneys through the ureters.
note: NIDDK: ureters connect kidneys to bladder and the bladder is a reservoir; StatPearls: lesser pelvis, storage reservoir; OpenStax: smooth muscle wall.

sentence: To empty it, the brain signals the sphincters to relax and the muscular wall to tighten, so that urine is pushed out through the urethra.
note: NIDDK: brain signals the sphincters to relax, then signals the muscular bladder wall to tighten, pushing urine out through the urethra.

sentence: Between emptyings the sphincter muscles stay contracted and keep the urethra closed.
note: NIDDK: sphincter muscles remain contracted to keep urine in the bladder while it fills; walls stay relaxed.

sentence: The urethra arises from the base of the bladder and carries urine out of the body.
note: OpenStax: urethra arises from the trigone area at the base of the bladder; NIDDK: urine leaves through the urethra.

sentence: Lesser pelvis behind the pubic symphysis in adults, rising into the abdomen as it fills
note: StatPearls: adult bladder sits in lesser pelvis when empty, rises into abdomen when full, directly behind pubic symphysis.

sentence: Urothelial lining, lamina propria, detrusor smooth muscle and an outer serosa or adventitia
note: StatPearls Histology: urothelial lining, lamina propria, muscularis propria (detrusor), outer serosa or adventitia.

sentence: Smooth triangle at the base formed by the two ureteric openings and the urethral opening; richest in sensory nerve receptors
note: OpenStax: smooth triangular area formed by two ureteral orifices and internal urethral orifice, with highest concentration of sensory receptors.

sentence: Involuntary internal sphincter of smooth muscle and voluntary external sphincter of skeletal muscle
note: OpenStax: involuntary internal sphincter of smooth muscle and voluntary external sphincter of skeletal muscle.

sentence: Superior and inferior vesical arteries, branches of the internal iliac arteries
note: StatPearls: superior and inferior vesical arteries are the main suppliers and both come from the internal iliac arteries.

sentence: Mostly to the external iliac nodes
note: StatPearls: bladder lymph mostly drains to the external iliac nodes.

sentence: Cystoscopy, a thin camera tube passed through the urethra into the bladder
note: NHS: a thin tube with a camera is put into the urethra and moved through it into the bladder.

sentence: In adults the bladder lies in the lesser pelvis when it is empty, directly behind the pubic symphysis, and rises into the abdomen as it fills.
note: StatPearls: sits in lesser pelvis when empty, rises into abdomen when full, directly behind the pubic symphysis.

sentence: It is described as having four parts: the apex or dome, the body, the fundus or base, and the neck.
note: StatPearls entry describes four parts: apex or dome, body, fundus, neck; fundus is the posteroinferior base.

sentence: Peritoneum covers the upper surface of the bladder.
note: OpenStax: bladder has peritoneum only over its dome; StatPearls: superior and part of posterior surfaces are peritoneum-covered.

sentence: Where a prostate is present, the base of the bladder is firmly attached to the prostate and the rectum lies behind.
note: OpenStax: in males bladder base is firmly attached to the base of the prostate; StatPearls: in males the rectum lies behind the bladder.

sentence: Where a vagina is present, the base of the bladder and the urethra rest on its anterior wall.
note: Returned text: in females the bladder base and urethra rest on the anterior vaginal wall; one review relates that wall to bladder base and urethra.

sentence: The muscles of the pelvic floor support the bladder from below.
note: StatPearls: pelvic floor muscles support the bladder from below.

sentence: Surgeons must identify the bladder during caesarean section to avoid injuring it.
note: StatPearls clinical note: surgeons must identify the bladder during caesarean sections to avoid injury.

sentence: The bladder wall has four layers: an inner urothelial lining, a lamina propria of connective tissue containing blood vessels and nerve endings, the detrusor muscle, and an outer serosa or adventitia.
note: StatPearls Histology: urothelium, lamina propria (connective tissue with vessels and nerve endings), muscularis propria (detrusor), serosa or adventitia.

sentence: The urothelium is thick when the bladder is relaxed and thins as the bladder fills, without structural damage.
note: StatPearls Histology: urothelium is thick when relaxed and thins in the distended bladder without structural damage.

sentence: The detrusor is made of crisscrossing bands of smooth muscle, with fibres arranged in spiral, longitudinal and circular bundles, and the whole organ is highly distensible.
note: OpenStax: highly distensible organ of crisscrossing smooth muscle bands (detrusor) with spiral, longitudinal and circular fibre bundles.

sentence: On the inner surface the trigone is a smooth triangular area formed by the two ureteric openings and the opening of the urethra.
note: OpenStax: trigone is a smooth triangular area formed by the two ureteral orifices and the internal urethral orifice.

sentence: It has the highest concentration of sensory nerve receptors in the bladder.
note: OpenStax: trigone has the highest concentration of sensory nerve receptors; StatPearls: most sensitive region for stretch receptors.

sentence: The trigone and the bladder neck are more firmly anchored to the tissue beneath and do not shrink as much during emptying or form rugae.
note: OpenStax: bladder neck and trigone are more firmly anchored to underlying tissue and do not shrink as significantly or form rugae.

sentence: The urethra begins at the trigone area at the base of the bladder.
note: OpenStax: urethra arises from the trigone area at the base of the bladder.

sentence: The male urethra also carries semen and is described in four regions: the preprostatic, prostatic, membranous and spongy or penile urethra.
note: OpenStax: male urethra has dual role carrying urine and semen; four regions preprostatic, prostatic, membranous, spongy or penile.

sentence: Two sphincters control the outflow of urine, and contracting them narrows the urethra to slow or stop urination.
note: StatPearls: urethra has internal and external sphincters; contracting them narrows the urethra to slow or stop urination.

sentence: The internal sphincter is smooth muscle, continuous with the detrusor, and works involuntarily; in the male urethra it also helps stop semen flowing back into the bladder during ejaculation.
note: StatPearls: internal sphincter is smooth muscle continuous with detrusor, involuntary, prevents semen reflux in males; OpenStax: involuntary smooth muscle.

sentence: The external sphincter is skeletal muscle under voluntary control and is supplied by the pudendal nerve.
note: OpenStax: voluntary external sphincter of skeletal muscle; StatPearls: external sphincter is supplied by the pudendal nerve.

sentence: Problems with the sphincters are commonly linked to urinary incontinence.
note: StatPearls clinical relevance: urinary incontinence is commonly linked to sphincter pathology.

sentence: The superior and inferior vesical arteries, branches of the internal iliac arteries, are the main arterial supply, with the superior vesical artery feeding the upper bladder.
note: StatPearls: superior and inferior vesical arteries from the internal iliac arteries are main suppliers; superior vesical feeds upper bladder.

sentence: Venous blood drains through the vesical venous plexus into the internal iliac veins, and lymph drains mostly to the external iliac nodes.
note: StatPearls: vesical venous plexus empties into internal iliac veins; lymph drains mostly to external iliac nodes.

sentence: Sympathetic and parasympathetic nerves arising from the pelvic plexus supply the bladder, together with somatic fibres.
note: StatPearls: bladder has sympathetic and parasympathetic innervation arising from the pelvic plexus; somatic fibres also involved.

sentence: Sympathetic activity, through the hypogastric nerves, suppresses contraction of the detrusor, whereas parasympathetic activity contracts the detrusor and relaxes the internal sphincter.
note: OpenStax: sympathetic activity via hypogastric nerves suppresses detrusor contraction; parasympathetic outflow contracts detrusor and relaxes internal sphincter.

sentence: Sensation from the upper wall travels with sympathetic fibres, and sensation from the lower wall with parasympathetic fibres.
note: StatPearls: sensation from the superior bladder wall travels with sympathetic fibres, from the inferior wall with parasympathetic fibres.

sentence: The bladder acts as both a storage reservoir and an excretory organ.
note: StatPearls: bladder acts as both a storage reservoir and an excretory organ.

sentence: Urination alternates between a storage phase, when urine collects, and a voiding phase, when the bladder empties.
note: StatPearls Physiology, Urination describes storage (bladder fills, detrusor relaxes) and voiding (detrusor contracts, sphincter opens) phases.

sentence: During storage the detrusor stays relaxed as the bladder fills, while the sphincter muscles stay contracted to keep urine in.
note: StatPearls: detrusor relaxes to allow storage; NIDDK: walls stay relaxed as bladder fills and sphincter muscles remain contracted.

sentence: Continuous sympathetic tone through the hypogastric nerve keeps the detrusor relaxed, and the pudendal nerve closes the external sphincter to support continence.
note: StatPearls: hypogastric nerve provides continuous sympathetic tone inducing detrusor relaxation; pudendal nerve closes the urethral sphincter to support continence.

sentence: Voiding starts when strong sensory signals from the bladder activate reflex pathways in the brainstem, including the pontine micturition centre, also known as Barrington's nucleus, which coordinates emptying.
note: StatPearls: intense afferent signals activate spinobulbospinal reflex pathways and the pontine micturition centre (Barrington's nucleus), which coordinates micturition.

sentence: The detrusor then contracts, the sphincters relax and urine flows out through the urethra.
note: StatPearls: detrusor contracts and urethral sphincter opens; NIDDK: brain signals sphincters to relax and the bladder wall to tighten.

sentence: Cystitis is a urinary tract infection that affects the bladder.
note: NHS: cystitis is a urinary tract infection (UTI) that affects the bladder.

sentence: It often gets better by itself, but may sometimes be treated with antibiotics.
note: NHS: it often gets better by itself, but may sometimes be treated with antibiotics.

sentence: Symptoms include pain or burning when passing urine, needing to go more often and urgently, dark, cloudy or strong-smelling urine, and pain low in the tummy.
note: NHS lists pain, burning or stinging on urinating, frequency and urgency, dark cloudy strong-smelling urine, and pain low in the tummy.

sentence: The shorter female urethra is linked to a higher incidence of bladder infections.
note: OpenStax: the shorter female urethra contributes to the higher incidence of bladder infections in females.

sentence: A more severe infection can cause pain in the back or side, particularly under the ribs, in the area of the kidneys.
note: NHS: when infection is more severe there may be pain in the back or side, particularly under the ribs, where the kidneys are.

sentence: The NHS says cystitis symptoms in children, and in people with a prostate, should always be assessed by a clinician.
note: NHS: children and men with cystitis symptoms should always be seen by a GP; less common and could be more serious in these groups.

sentence: Bladder pain syndrome, or interstitial cystitis, is a chronic condition in which pain usually worsens as the bladder fills and eases after urinating; severity ranges from mild discomfort to intense pain.
note: NIDDK: pain usually gets worse as the bladder fills and better after urinating; some feel mild discomfort or pressure, others intense bladder pain.

sentence: The NHS describes several types of urinary incontinence.
note: NHS lists stress, urge, overflow, total and mixed urinary incontinence.

sentence: In stress incontinence urine leaks when the bladder is put under sudden extra pressure, for example by coughing, sneezing or heavy lifting.
note: NHS: stress incontinence is leaking urine when the bladder is put under sudden extra pressure, e.g. coughing, sneezing, laughing, heavy lifting.

sentence: Urge incontinence is leakage linked to a sudden, strong need to pass urine and often occurs with overactive bladder syndrome, in which the bladder muscle is more active than usual.
note: NHS: urge incontinence is leakage linked to a sudden strong need to pee, often with overactive bladder syndrome (bladder muscle more active than usual).

sentence: Most bladder cancers begin in the urothelial cells that line the urinary tract.
note: NCI: urothelial carcinoma (transitional cell carcinoma) is the most common bladder cancer and begins in urothelial cells lining the urinary tract.

sentence: Blood in the urine is the commonest warning sign; it may look pink, red or dark brown, may come and go, or may show up only on a laboratory test.
note: NHS: blood in pee may be pink, red or dark brown; NCI: commonest warning sign, may come and go or show only on lab tests.

sentence: It is usually caused by something other than cancer, such as infection or stones, but the NHS advises that it should be assessed by a clinician even when there are no other symptoms.
note: NCI: blood in urine is usually caused by other conditions such as infections or stones; NHS: get blood in pee assessed even without other symptoms.

sentence: Cystoscopy lets a clinician look at the lining of the bladder.
note: NHS: a thin tube with a camera is used and the clinician looks around the lining of the bladder.

sentence: A thin tube with a camera is gently passed into the urethra and moved through it into the bladder.
note: NHS: the tube is gently put into the urethra and moved through it into the bladder.

sentence: Saline is run into the bladder to inflate it, which makes it easier to see inside, and local anaesthetic gel numbs the urethra beforehand.
note: NHS: saline is pumped in to inflate the bladder so it is easier to see inside; local anaesthetic gel numbs the urethra.

sentence: The ureteric openings can also be seen at cystoscopy.
note: StatPearls clinical note: cystoscopy can show the ureteric openings.

sentence: For suspected bladder cancer the NCI describes starting with a urine sample, with cystoscopy and imaging ordered if needed, and diagnosis and staging usually begin with cystoscopy.
note: NCI: doctors typically start with a urine sample and may order cystoscopy and imaging; diagnosis and staging usually begin with cystoscopy.
